# OpenCodeLocator

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.OpenCode` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Editor/OpenCode/OpenCodeLocator.cs#L13)

Finds the opencode executable on this machine.
npm installs a shim next to the real binary rather than the binary itself - on Windows the
thing on PATH is opencode.cmd, and launching a .cmd means launching cmd.exe, whose child we
could no longer kill directly. So the shim is only ever used as a signpost: when one is
found we resolve the real executable beside it and spawn that.

### Resolve() {#resolve}

Absolute path to the opencode executable, or null when it is not installed.
An explicit path in preferences always wins so a developer can point at a build of their
own without touching PATH.
